failure_summary.description: Personal names were over-normalized: an established public name was replaced with a formal variant, and a descriptive rank was added to the name.
The answer used a later company brand instead of the historically relevant name, despite existing guidance against that substitution.

patch.reasoning: Clarify that a person’s conventional identifying name is not necessarily their formal given-name variant, and that a rank supplied descriptively is not automatically part of the answer. The later-brand distinction is already covered, so it needs no separate new rule.

edits.target: For proper names and titles, use the conventional form that identifies the requested entity. Do not substitute a nickname or later brand name for the historically relevant label, omit words from a work's title when the work is requested, or add optional middle names. Conversely, when the clue requests a generic class, do not embellish it with a narrower associated name.
edits.content: For proper names and titles, use the conventional designation for the entity in the historical or contextual frame asked about; do not assume a formal given-name variant is preferable to an established public name, and do not substitute a later brand name for the historically relevant label. Do not append a rank, honorific, or status supplied only as a description unless it is conventionally part of the requested name. Retain words intrinsic to a work's title when the work is requested, and avoid optional middle names. Conversely, when the clue requests a generic class, do not embellish it with a narrower associated name.

edits.target: For people, use the full identity supported by substantive context; do not answer with only a surname merely because a clue echo abbreviates it. Preserve initials, titles, and other name elements when the clue or a reliable passage supplies them—do not strip them for stylistic normalization.
edits.content: For people, use a conventional identifying name supported by substantive context; do not answer with only a surname merely because a clue echo abbreviates it. Do not expand an established public name to a different formal given-name variant or append a descriptive title or rank just because a clue or passage supplies it. Include initials or titles when they are part of the identifying name requested, not merely descriptive.
